question: Which three areas come together to make up nursing informatics?
explanation: You've got this! Nursing informatics simply blends nursing practice with computer and information technology to help us manage patient data much better. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is informatics so helpful in everyday nursing practice?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for direct patient contact
options.B: It reduces the total number of hospital beds needed
options.C: It replaces the role of doctors in diagnosing illnesses
options.D: It improves how clinical data is managed and communicated

explanation: Think of informatics as your handy digital assistant. It helps healthcare teams share accurate patient updates quickly and smoothly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: What does the word 'interoperability' mean when talking about electronic health records?

options.A: Computers automatically print out paper charts
options.B: Different health systems share patient data safely
options.C: Nurses can log in without a secure password
options.D: Patients can update their own medical diagnosis

explanation: Interoperability is just a big word meaning different hospitals or clinics can talk to each other and share patient records securely. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: What kind of details will you typically find inside an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: Personal social media activity and contacts
options.B: Only the patient's current financial billing statements
options.C: Comprehensive medical history and clinical data

explanation: An EHR holds a complete digital story of a patient's health journey across different visits and treatments. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: What was one of the biggest headaches with traditional paper charts?

options.A: They could be accessed simultaneously from abroad
options.B: They required continuous electricity to remain legible
options.C: Only one person could view them at a time
options.D: They updated themselves automatically every hour

explanation: Paper files can only be in one place at once, causing delays when two different clinicians need the same chart simultaneously! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: How do digital records help solve the age-old problem of messy handwriting?

options.A: By translating foreign languages into local dialects
options.B: By deleting unsigned medical notes automatically
options.C: By replacing handwritten notes with clear typed text
options.D: By converting verbal orders into written prescriptions

explanation: Typed text is easy for everyone to read, which drastically cuts down on medication errors caused by misread doctor notes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: In health tech, what do the letters CPOE stand for?
explanation: CPOE is simply the digital system doctors and other providers use to send test and treatment orders straight to the team. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of Clinical Decision Support tools in hospital software?

options.A: To schedule nursing shifts for the upcoming month
options.B: To calculate monthly hospital electricity bills
options.C: To market new pharmaceutical products to patients
options.D: To provide automated alerts regarding drug allergies

explanation: These smart tools act like a safety net, popping up with quick warnings if a prescribed drug clashes with a patient's allergies. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which type of digital system is usually limited to just one specific clinic or hospital?
explanation: An EMR (Electronic Medical Record) acts mainly as the digital chart for one particular facility, unlike an EHR which travels further. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the biggest superpower an EHR has over a standard EMR?

options.A: It prevents patients from viewing their own labs
options.B: It shares data across multiple healthcare organizations
options.C: It requires no computer hardware or electricity
options.D: It functions without any internet connection

explanation: EHRs are designed to share information smoothly across different hospitals, labs, and pharmacies so patient history is never lost. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is a direct benefit of using digital health records?

options.A: Complete elimination of nursing shift handovers
options.B: Faster retrieval of patient lab results
options.D: Automatic diagnosis of complex medical conditions

explanation: No more running down to the lab! Digital systems pop test results right onto the screen as soon as they are ready. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: During an emergency, a nurse needs to quickly check a patient's past allergy to penicillin. What makes this super easy in an EHR?

options.A: Instant access to historical clinical data
options.B: Direct video calling with hospital administrators
options.C: Printed shift reports left at the nurse's desk
options.D: Automatic billing generation for pharmacy services

explanation: Having patient history stored centrally means life-saving allergy information is just a click away when seconds count. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is a major everyday challenge for digital health systems here in Nigeria?

options.A: An absolute lack of trained nurses

explanation: Frequent power fluctuations and outages can disrupt computers and servers, making reliable backup power a must in our hospitals. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why might some experienced healthcare workers initially feel hesitant about switching to EHRs?

options.A: Habit and comfort with traditional paper charting
options.B: Lack of basic reading and writing literacy
options.C: Preference for writing prescriptions on walls
options.D: Mandatory retirement upon touching a computer

explanation: Change can be tough! When you are used to pen and paper for years, moving to screens requires patience, encouragement, and good training. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which of these habits helps protect patient privacy at a busy nurses' station?

options.A: Logging off the computer when leaving the area
options.B: Sharing your personal password with student nurses
options.C: Leaving patient medical records open on public desks
options.D: Writing access codes on sticky notes near the screen

explanation: Always lock your screen when you walk away. It is a simple habit that keeps confidential patient info safe from curious eyes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of role-based access control in hospital software?

options.A: To hide doctor orders from the nursing staff
options.B: To give every hospital employee full administrative rights
options.C: To restrict data viewing to job-relevant duties
options.D: To block patients from ever viewing their own vitals

explanation: Role-based security ensures that staff members only see the specific patient details they need to do their jobs properly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: As a bedside nurse, which of these tasks will you typically do on an EHR system?

options.A: Documenting vital signs and medication administration
options.B: Purchasing new computer servers for the hospital
options.C: Writing the underlying software programming code
options.D: Repairing broken electrical sockets in patient rooms

explanation: You'll spend time recording your patient assessments, vital signs, and meds directly into the digital chart as part of your daily care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h9)

question: You notice a colleague accidentally typed a wrong medication dose into the EHR. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Ignore the mistake since computers rarely make errors
options.B: Wait until patient discharge to mention the issue
options.C: Delete the entire patient record to clear the error
options.D: Report and correct the discrepancy following facility protocol

explanation: Mistakes happen! The safest approach is to follow your hospital's procedure to report and fix the record right away so patient safety stays protected. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h9)
